scope: Proposition 6.1 of the manuscript “Compatibility entropy and the spectrum of a Thorp sweep” (preprints/Compatibility-entropy-and-the-spectrum-of-a-Thorp-sweep-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dae8f5ca5b99fbec), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 26. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let n = qm, with m ≤ q ≤ 2m and m sufficiently large. On a q × m grid choose all row and column permutations independently. Relative to uniform in each line, suppose their laws have bounded densities, and let LR, LC be the sums for rows and columns, respectively, of the logarithms of these density bounds. Consider the product of the row permutation layer and then the column permutation layer. Call the product reversible in order if it can also be written as a column layer followed by a row layer (this just refers to a factorization of a permutation). With C an absolute constant, Pr(reversible in order) ≤ exp  −n + n0.58 + C log n (LR + LC)  . (30)
